\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انگریز} (angrez)}{انگریز (angrez)}]{\ur{انگریز} (angrez) — an English person}

\label{lesson:UR-C313-angrez}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a rebellion, then the Urdu for to challenge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انگریز}}
\textbf{\ur{انگریز}} — \emph{angrez} — \textquotedblleft{}an English person\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{انگریز} \ur{سو} \ur{سال} \ur{یہاں} \ur{رہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{angrez sau sāl yahāṅ rahe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The English stayed here for a hundred years.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انگریز}} (\emph{angrez}) is usually traced to Portuguese \emph{inglês}, \textquotedblleft{}English\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian \emph{angrez}. \textbf{\ur{انگریزی}} is the language.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{angrez}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{angrez}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{angrez sau sāl yahāṅ rahe.} — The English stayed here for a hundred years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a rebellion, then the Urdu for to challenge, then say \emph{angrez} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{انگریز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An English person\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تحریک} (tahrīk)}{تحریک (tahrīk)}]{\ur{تحریک} (tahrīk) — a movement (of people)}

\label{lesson:UR-C313-tahrik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to challenge, then the Urdu for an English person.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تحریک}}
\textbf{\ur{تحریک}} — \emph{tahrīk} — \textquotedblleft{}a movement (of people)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہر} \ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{آزادی} \ur{کی} \ur{تحریک} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{har shahr meṅ āzādī kī tahrīk thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a freedom movement in every city.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تحریک}} (\emph{tahrīk}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taḥrīk}, \textquotedblleft{}a setting in motion\textquotedblright{}: people moved to act together.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جدوجہد} (jaddojahd)}{جدوجہد (jaddojahd)}]{\ur{جدوجہد} (jaddojahd) — a struggle}

\label{lesson:UR-C313-jaddojahd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an English person, then the Urdu for a movement (of people).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جدوجہد}}
\textbf{\ur{جدوجہد}} — \emph{jaddojahd} — \textquotedblleft{}a struggle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{لمبی} \ur{جدوجہد} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih ek lambī jaddojahd thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It was a long struggle.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جدوجہد}} (\emph{jaddojahd}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{jidd}, \textquotedblleft{}effort\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{jahd}, \textquotedblleft{}striving\textquotedblright{}, joined by \emph{o}, \textquotedblleft{}and\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قربانی} (qurbānī)}{قربانی (qurbānī)}]{\ur{قربانی} (qurbānī) — a sacrifice}

\label{lesson:UR-C313-qurbani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a movement (of people), then the Urdu for a struggle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قربانی}}
\textbf{\ur{قربانی}} — \emph{qurbānī} — \textquotedblleft{}a sacrifice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوگوں} \ur{نے} \ur{بڑی} \ur{قربانیاں} \ur{دیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{logoṅ ne baṛī qurbāniyāṅ dīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People made great sacrifices.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قربانی}} (\emph{qurbānī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qurbān}, \textquotedblleft{}an offering\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}. It is also the animal sacrifice of Eid.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سونپنا} (saunpnā)}{سونپنا (saunpnā)}]{\ur{سونپنا} (saunpnā) — to entrust; to hand over}

\label{lesson:UR-C313-saunpna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a struggle, then the Urdu for a sacrifice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سونپنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سونپنا}} — \emph{saunpnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to entrust; to hand over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بادشاہ} \ur{نے} \ur{بیٹے} \ur{کو} \ur{تخت} \ur{سونپا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bādshāh ne beṭe ko takht saunpā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The king handed the throne to his son.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{چابی} \ur{سونپی}, \emph{us ne chābī saunpī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سونپنا}} (\emph{saunpnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{saũpnā}, \textquotedblleft{}hands over\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sámarpayati} (CDIAL 13192). The one who receives takes \textbf{\ur{کو}}, and the verb follows the thing: \textbf{\ur{تخت} \ur{سونپا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saunpnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bādshāh ne beṭe ko takht saunpā.} — The king handed the throne to his son.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a struggle, then the Urdu for a sacrifice, then say \emph{saunpnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
